subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 landed the ONE derivation of an elementary item's EFFECTIVE usage -- its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing group's (13.18.60.4 GR1) -- feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and EVERY 13.18.60.3 screen through the SAME code the written-clause path runs (PictureAnalyzer.ScreenUsageAgainstPicture, extracted for the purpose). The invariant is stated and locked as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as cases: `01 G USAGE u. 05 A <pic>.` and `01 G. 05 A <pic> USAGE u.` are the same item, so they must produce the same verdict, the same diagnostic code and the same width, for EVERY member of the Usage enum. UsageInheritanceDriftTests enumerates the enum and asserts exactly that (24 members x 6 pictures x 2 arms). MEASURED on the pre-fix tree 39479e19: 108 of those 138 cells DIFFERED between the two arms; after the fix, 0 differ. SR2 HAD NO SITE AT ALL before this landing (`grep '13.18.60.3 SR2' src/` was empty): the nearer clause simply won and the outer one was discarded in silence, so `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 A PIC 9(4). 05 B PIC 9(4) USAGE DISPLAY.` compiled with B a 4-byte DISPLAY item and the group 6 bytes where the conforming spelling gives 4. It is now COBOL1927, reported against the SUBORDINATE entry and against the NEAREST enclosing entry that wrote a clause, so a chain G->H->A reports each adjacent contradiction once, at the entry whose clause has to change. "The same usage" is compared as the RESOLVED Usage member, which is what the standard asks: SR6 makes COMP the abbreviation for COMPUTATIONAL, and GR4/GR6 leave the BINARY and COMPUTATIONAL representations to the implementor, so this implementation's identification of the three makes them one usage and `USAGE COMP` inside a `USAGE BINARY` group conforms -- pinned positively by the second half of the Sr2_ContradictingUsages test (A=2 B=2 C=2 G=6). Edition-invariant: a group-level USAGE clause, COMPUTATIONAL and DISPLAY are all COBOL-85, which is why the negative golden's reject-at names all four editions.
